hooks.text: If you are not getting leads every day, this video is for you. Most businesses' number one problem is not the product. It is leads.
I polished an app for a year and nobody came. Then one shift brought leads every day and a 300k sale. Here is the shift.
Everyone tells you to build first. Dead wrong. Build first is a trap, and I paid tens of thousands of dollars to learn why.
There is a second cost to having no leads, and it is bigger than the sales you are missing. It is your price.
Pick one platform, fix one profile, leave three comments. That is how 8k followers in 8 months started.

sections.heading: Stick with this and you leave with
sections.image_alt: Sketch of a mailbox overflowing with envelopes beside a calendar where every day holds an envelope, titled LEADS EVERY DAY
bullets: Why you have no leads, and the one thing most advice gets backwards.
The audience-first shift and how to find the best kind of leads: a premium offer.
A simple short form system that brings leads every day, from one platform.
Two real results from this exact approach: 8k followers in 8 months, and a 300k sale.

key.text: If you are not getting leads every day, this is for you.

sections.question: What costs you more than the sales you are missing when you have no leads?

sections.heading: Most businesses lack leads, and the usual advice makes it worse

beats.heading: The number one problem is leads, not product
beats.image_alt: Sketch of an open storefront with an empty street and a tumbleweed, titled NO LEADS

crowd: Start by designing the product or service.
Get it polished, then they will come.
me: Dead wrong. Build first is a trap.
Most businesses' number one problem: no leads.

beats.heading: Build first is a trap
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a person happily building inside a mousetrap-shaped cage while a crowd waits down the path, titled BUILD TRAP
bullets: Building feels good. Dopamine hits every time you ship a piece.
That good feeling becomes procrastination. It keeps you from leads and sales.

key.text: Building is the most productive-looking way to avoid selling.

beats.question: If building is the trap, what did I do instead that turned into a 300k sale?

beats.label: Story
beats.heading: If I build it, they will come
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a polished app on a launch stage facing empty chairs while money bags fly away, titled NOBODY CAME
bullets: Built an app, polished it for a year. No one cared.
Tens of thousands of dollars spent: hired people, outsourced leads to "marketers". It did not work.
story: Struggled with this for years, believing: if I build it, they will come.
A couple of years ago: one app, a year of polish, zero interest.
Frustration led to spending tens of thousands trying to buy a fix: hires, outsourced "marketers".
The lesson that came out of it: start with the audience, before any service or product.

key.text: A year of polish. Tens of thousands spent. Zero audience.

beats.heading: The hidden second cost of no leads: your price
beats.image_alt: Split sketch of a water truck on an empty beach with a falling price and one cooler on a packed beach with a rising price, titled BEACH WATER

crowd: Price is set by the market. Compete on price.
me: Supply and demand is micro economics, and you control it.
More demand than supply, the price goes up.

bullets: Beach one: truck full of water, other sellers, ten people on the sand. Charge little.
Beach two: packed beach, one cooler of ice cold bottles, only seller. Charge more.

key.text: Generate more demand than supply and the price goes up.

sections.heading: Audience first, then a premium offer, then short form leads every day

beats.label: The shift
beats.heading: Start with the audience, before any product or service
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a large crowd numbered 1 with an arrow to a small product box numbered 2, titled AUDIENCE FIRST
bullets: What are you selling, what problem are you solving, if you do not start with the audience?
The audience tells you what to build and who pays for it.

beats.label: Who to attract
beats.heading: Four types of audience, one premium offer
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a two by two grid with the painful and specific cell circled and a crown labeled RICH, titled PREMIUM OFFER
bullets: Two axes: optional vs painful. General vs specific.
Target the corner: the most painful, most specific problem you can solve.
For the richest people you can solve it for.
That is a premium offer. It is the key to success. Works in any niche.

beats.label: Example
beats.heading: A mentee in the health niche
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a target with a single arrow in the bullseye next to a person with a CEO name tag, titled ONE PAINFUL PROBLEM
bullets: Health, to weight loss, to loss of visceral fat. That specific.
CEOs and wealthy individuals first. He is doing it and starting to see success.

beats.label: The map
beats.heading: Three sources of daily leads
beats.image_alt: Sketch of three pipes labeled SHORT FORM, REFERRALS and RENTED pouring into one bucket, titled THREE SOURCES
bullets: 1. Short form content.
2. High trust referral leads.
3. Rented leads: affiliates, partnerships, paid ads.
Today: short form. The other two another day.
beats.question: Why will your short form posts never ask anyone to buy anything?

beats.label: Step one
beats.heading: Pick one platform. Just one.
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a hand pointing at one phone in a row of five, the chosen one circled in red, titled PICK ONE
bullets: TikTok, Instagram, X, Facebook, Threads, YouTube Shorts.
The one you are most comfortable on, ideally one you already use daily.
Every platform has a culture. Go against the flow and you read as the used car salesman.
Weigh where your ideal clients hang out, including age demographics.
Not on social yet? Start now. Follow, comment, support others before posting.

key.text: One platform, the one you already live on.

beats.question: How did 8k followers in 8 months come from comments, not posts?

beats.label: Step two
beats.heading: Set up a professional profile
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a phone profile page with banner, avatar and a circled link icon at the top, titled LINK IN BIO
bullets: Community-professional bio, banner and photo where supported.
Main link at the top of the bio or profile.
Now "see the link in my bio" works, every time.

beats.label: Step three
beats.heading: Research outliers: the magic quadrant
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a scatter chart with one large dot in the upper right circled and labeled OUTLIER, with an hourglass, titled MAGIC QUADRANT
bullets: Tool: Eden, link in the description. Finds trending topics that are outliers on any platform.
An outlier is the algorithm's signal: this creator uniquely met demand in that moment.
Perishable. Supply catches up and the algorithm moves on.
Rule: 3x or more outliers, within a week of posting. The magic quadrant, video linked above.

key.text: 3x outlier, under a week old. Fresh signal only.

beats.label: Step four
beats.heading: Tear the winners down
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a video frame taken apart on a workbench under a magnifying glass, titled TEAR DOWN
bullets: Study packaging, format, method of delivery, images and thumbnails.
Do not copy. Do not reinvent the wheel either.
Use them as a guide. Add your taste and point of view.
To break through: say something new, and above all, useful.

beats.label: Step five
beats.heading: Four parts of content that works
beats.image_alt: Sketch of four stacked blocks labeled HOOK, BODY, WIN and CTA, titled FOUR PARTS
bullets: Hook: the promise. Body: the value. Win: a small insight or tool. CTA.
Short form is no different, just tighter. Tear down any winner and the four are there.

key.text: Hook, body, win, CTA. Even in 30 seconds.

beats.label: The rule
beats.heading: The CTA is never "buy my thing"
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a well, a gift box with an envelope, and a crossed-out price tag, titled FREE FIRST

crowd: Every post should sell. Always pitch the offer.
me: People do not like being sold on short form. Sell there and you poison your well.
Point to something free to capture the email, or to a long form piece.

key.text: Sell on short form and you poison the well.

beats.label: Hack
beats.heading: Comment early, add value
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a viral post with a rocket, a comment bubble holding a lightbulb and an early clock, titled EARLY COMMENT
bullets: Be early on others' posts that go viral.
Add real value. Not "I agree", not "good post".
People notice, check the bio, click the link.

beats.label: Proof
beats.heading: 8k followers in 8 months, leads every day
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a rising chart made of people icons ending at a clubhouse door with envelopes, titled 8K IN 8 MONTHS
bullets: Adding value and supporting others: 8k followers on X in 8 months.
Pointed them to a free Skool community, later paid for new members. Every email captured.
From that audience: leads every day, now.

key.text: Free community, emails captured, then paid. Leads daily.

beats.label: Proof
beats.heading: The 300k sale: audience first, again
beats.image_alt: Sketch of a handshake between a person holding a prototype and a person in front of a large crowd, with a money bag, titled 300K
bullets: Product idea, no audience. Built a prototype only.
Asked a creator with the audience to be an affiliate. They bought the site instead: 200k, then 100k more, still going.
story: Had an idea for a product and realized there was no audience for it. Refused to repeat the old mistake.
Built a prototype, nothing more. Reached out to someone with a large audience in that niche.
Offer: be an affiliate, earn commissions for sending leads. Their answer: no, they wanted to buy the site.
200k for the site, then another 100k of improvements and maintenance, and still going.
Feedback from that audience came fast. Functionality and value were added quickly.
You can leverage someone else's audience to establish value and win. One way or another, the audience comes first.

key.text: Prototype only. Borrowed audience. 300k and counting.

sections.heading: A first win in under an hour
sections.image_alt: Sketch of a clipboard with three ticked boxes labeled PICK, PROFILE and COMMENT and a stopwatch, titled TODAY

steps.title: Pick your one platform
steps.text: The one already on your phone that you open daily. Decide now, not after research.

steps.title: Fix the profile in ten minutes
steps.text: Photo, banner, one clear bio line, and your main link at the top.

steps.title: Leave three valuable comments
steps.text: Find three posts in your niche taking off today. Add a real insight to each. No "great post".

steps.title: Write one short post in four parts
steps.text: Hook, body, one small win, and a CTA that points to something free.

key.text: Profile clicks start the same day you add value early.

sections.heading: What we covered
bullets: No leads is the number one problem. Build first is a trap.
Audience first, then a premium offer: painful, specific, rich.
More demand than supply and your price goes up.
Three lead sources. Short form first: one platform, profile, outliers, teardown, four parts, free CTA, early comments.
Proof: 8k in 8 months, and a 300k sale with a borrowed audience.
